deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down. Behind it are faint pencil sketches of zig-zag paths that seem unrelated. The ink notes are a small counting sketch for an arrangement of n pseudo-lines (n pseudo-lines in a disk, or in the projective plane). This fits the theme of cote 154 (systèmes de pseudo-droites) and the neighbouring drawings (pp. 82 and 84: disks crossed by pseudo-lines, shaded bands, a distinguished dashed pseudo-line).

1. Two-pencil figure. A pseudo-line L carries two multiple points p and p'. Through p pass nu pseudo-lines (L plus nu-1 others), and through p' pass nu' (L plus nu'-1 others). In a pseudo-line arrangement two distinct curves meet exactly once. Since L already joins p and p', no other curve passes through both points. So the two pencils share only L.

2. Counting. The formulas count the curves of the arrangement that meet L away from p and p', or that cross a band or segment attached to L. For example, n-1 curves other than L, minus (nu-1) and (nu'-1), leaves n+1-nu-nu' curves crossing L at other points. The last line, n - x - (nu-1) - (nu'-1) + x, has two x-terms struck through: they cancel, leaving n - (nu-1) - (nu'-1). The first expression, 2n - [(nu-1)+(nu'-1)], looks like a count taken twice, e.g. over two sides of L or two boundaries of a band. A curly brace above it groups terms. The line '= n - (nu'-1)' looks like a partial simplification under an assumption not shown on the page.

3. Rectangle figure. A rectangle with tick marks along its top side, labelled at both ends (probably nu and nu'), with a thin wedge-shaped strip below. This seems to schematise the segment or band along L between p and p', with ticks marking the crossings by other pseudo-lines. The strip below shows the band degenerating to a thin sliver.

4. Disk figure. A circle crossed by about seven pseudo-lines, one traced in orange as the distinguished curve. This matches the 'dashed central pseudo-line' and shaded band of p. 84.

Overall, this is elementary bookkeeping on incidences and crossings in pseudo-line arrangements, probably in service of a local modification (moving or sweeping a pseudo-line, or shrinking a band) used to classify or deform arrangements.
errors: The chain as transcribed, 2n - [(nu-1)+(nu'-1)] = n - (nu'-1), is not an identity in general. It would need n = nu - 1 or some unstated context, so it is either a partial or conditional step or two separate computations, not one equality.
The page gives no definition of what is being counted, so the reconstruction of the counting is conjectural.

ideas.what: Counting the pseudo-lines through two multiple points on a common pseudo-line, using that two pseudo-lines meet exactly once, so the pencils at p and p' share only L
ideas.modern_name: Incidence/crossing count in pseudo-line arrangements (Levi; Grünbaum's Arrangements and Spreads)

ideas.what: Band or strip along a distinguished pseudo-line, with crossings marked (rectangle with ticks degenerating to a wedge)
ideas.modern_name: Sweeping or mutation of a pseudo-line through an arrangement (triangle flips / wiring-diagram sweeps)

deep.surprise_reason: These are fragmentary, routine incidence counts and sketches for pseudo-line arrangements. Nothing on the page goes beyond standard combinatorics, and no result is completed.

The rectangle carries end-labels that look like nu and nu' (upside down); these are not in the machine transcription.
A curly brace sits above the expression 2n - [(nu-1)+(nu'-1)].
In the last line, n - x - (nu-1) - (nu'-1) + x, both x-terms are struck through (cancelled), not just bracketed.
